mechanism: Auth store reads localStorage 'token' and 'username' at initialization (lines ~33-34) and writes them on login (lines ~38-39); no server round trip is required to consider the client authenticated on load.
expected_behavior: Pre-setting localStorage 'token'/'username' before a page load causes the app to treat the session as already authenticated; navigating straight to a protected route (e.g. /checkout) skips the Login screen.
notes: Confirms the mechanism documented in SUT01-EV-0001.

mechanism: README Test Users table documents performance_glitch_user: 'API delay (~3s)'.
expected_behavior: All API calls made as performance_glitch_user are delayed by about 3 seconds.
notes: Candidate identification only; see SUT01-EV-0015 for exact source-verified figure.

mechanism: apply_user_behavior() calls time.sleep(3.0) synchronously before returning the user when behavior == 'performance_glitch'; this dependency gates every endpoint that requires an authenticated user's behavior to be applied (e.g. GET /api/pizzas, POST /api/checkout).
expected_behavior: Every request from performance_glitch_user through an endpoint depending on apply_user_behavior is delayed by exactly 3.0 seconds server-side, deterministically, on every call.

mechanism: GET /api/debug/latency-spike sleeps a random 0.5-5.0s and reports the exact delay applied; GET /api/debug/cpu-load runs a fixed, expensive recursive fibonacci(35) computation server-side and reports measured duration. Neither endpoint requires authentication.
expected_behavior: GET /api/debug/latency-spike returns after a randomized 0.5-5.0s delay with the applied delay_seconds value in the response body; GET /api/debug/cpu-load returns after a fixed heavy computation with duration_seconds in the response body.
notes: latency-spike's delay is randomized within a documented range (stochastic degradation, distinct from performance_glitch_user's deterministic 3.0s in SUT01-EV-0015); cpu-load's workload is fixed/deterministic but wall-clock duration depends on host hardware (time/environment-dependent).

mechanism: When behavior == 'a11y_glitch', GET /api/pizzas and GET /api/cart pick one of exactly 3 documented modes at random per call (missing_name: field becomes ''; wrong_lang: a different language's text is substituted; extreme_text: text is repeated 15x) and apply it to each item's name/description fields server-side.
expected_behavior: A given call to GET /api/pizzas as a11y_glitch_user returns every pizza's name/description mutated by exactly one of the three enumerated modes (the same mode for all items in that call).
notes: Mode selection is random per call (random.choice), so the specific mode is not fixed in advance, though the finite set of 3 possible outcomes is fully known/documented in source; recorded under cross-cutting property Determinism as stochastic.

mechanism: When behavior == 'problem', both catalog and cart items are forced to price=0.0 and image='https://broken-image-url.com/404.jpg' deterministically, replacing the normal converted price and product photo.
expected_behavior: Every catalog/cart screenshot taken while logged in as problem_user shows $0.00 prices and a broken/placeholder product image on every item, versus standard_user's normal priced, photographed items — a stable, repeatable visual difference a screenshot-diff tool can capture on demand.
notes: Tie-break rule applied at the cell level (audit.md section 3, Visual Testing): confirmed_score=2, provisional_score=3 retained as an unresolved candidate, per protocol/capability-rubric-v1.md "Tie-break rule for undecidable adjacent scores." Unresolved verification requirement: this record establishes a controlled DATA condition (price/image fields) that happens to render visibly differently, not a mechanism the SUT itself frames as a visual-testing condition as such; confirming Score 3 would need either a mechanism that establishes a specifically visual perturbation (e.g. a controlled layout, contrast, or rendering condition), or an EXECUTION_VERIFIED screenshot-diff run demonstrating this condition produces a stable, tool-detectable visual difference against a baseline.

mechanism: POST /api/profile's own docstring states its purpose: 'seed here to pin a reproducible value before a visual-regression snapshot'; seed_user_profile replaces the profile with default values overlaid by only the supplied fields, so the result depends only on the call, not on prior state.
expected_behavior: Seeding the profile via POST /api/profile with a fixed payload, then rendering the Profile screen, is expected to produce a pixel-stable render across repeated seed+snapshot cycles (modulo non-deterministic chrome such as the system clock, if displayed).
notes: The auditor searched frontend/package.json and frontend/cypress for a screenshot-diff/comparison tool (Percy, pixelmatch, cypress-image-snapshot) and found none wired in at this commit; recorded in limitations.md as a tooling gap, not a capability deduction (generic tool presence/absence does not move the rubric score either direction). Same tie-break disposition as SUT01-EV-0020 (Visual Testing: confirmed_score=2, provisional_score=3 unresolved candidate); this record documents stated intent for reproducible snapshots but is not itself a visual-perturbation mechanism or an executed screenshot comparison.

mechanism: README Test Users table documents security_glitch_user: 'XSS profile + IDOR + leaks'.
expected_behavior: This user exhibits a poisoned profile, an unauthorized-order-access bypass, and checkout errors with leaked internal details.
notes: Candidate identification only; see SUT01-EV-0023/0024/0025 for source verification of the three distinct mechanisms.

mechanism: Both GET /api/orders/{order_id} and PATCH /api/orders/{order_id} check `order["username"] != current_user["username"] and current_user["behavior"] != "security_glitch"` before returning 403 — meaning security_glitch_user is explicitly exempted from the ownership check on both endpoints.
expected_behavior: Logging in as security_glitch_user and requesting GET or PATCH /api/orders/{order_id} for an order created by a different user returns 200 with that order's data (including PATCH being able to cancel someone else's pending order), instead of the 403 every other authenticated user receives for the same request — a documented, reproducible IDOR (insecure direct object reference) condition.
notes: Unambiguous, deterministic bypass condition; the primary confirming mechanism for this modality's Score 3.

mechanism: On login, security_glitch_user has one of 3 profile fields (full_name/address/notes) seeded server-side with one of 3 canned script/attribute-injection payloads, unsanitized; GET /api/users/me/profile returns the field verbatim.
expected_behavior: GET /api/users/me/profile for a security_glitch_user session returns a profile field containing a raw, unescaped script/event-handler payload string (e.g. '<script>alert(''xss-test'')</script>') — detectable by an API-level security scanner as unsanitized input persistence.
notes: The auditor searched frontend/src for dangerouslySetInnerHTML and found none; the web client renders profile fields as literal React JSX text, which React escapes by default. This condition was NOT verified to execute as a working client-side XSS in the web UI as currently rendered — it is SOURCE_VERIFIED only as an API-level unsanitized-persistence condition. Does not by itself change the cell's confirmed_score: SUT01-EV-0023 (IDOR) already independently confirms Score 3 for this modality.

mechanism: should_trigger_error() returns True with probability 0.5 for behavior in ('error','security_glitch'); for security_glitch, the checkout endpoint then raises HTTP 500 with one of 3 canned messages that leak implementation details (a stack trace, a DB host+credentials-adjacent string, and a missing-secret-file path).
expected_behavior: Roughly half of POST /api/checkout calls made as security_glitch_user return HTTP 500 with one of the three enumerated leak-style messages instead of a generic error.
notes: Trigger rate is probabilistic (~50%), not a fixed single outcome per call; the full set of 3 possible leaked messages is enumerated in source.
